title: Dataset of an EEG-based BCI experiment in Virtual Reality using P300
description: This dataset comprises electroencephalographic recordings from 21 healthy subjects performing a visual P300-based brain-computer interface task in two environments: a personal computer and a virtual reality headset. The study compares BCI performance and user experience across these modalities using a 6×6 matrix speller paradigm with 16-channel EEG acquisition at 512 Hz. The dataset includes 12 experimental blocks per session with randomized target and non-target visual stimuli, enabling investigation of P300 event-related potentials and BCI efficacy in immersive versus traditional computing contexts. Artificial random feedback (70% expected accuracy) was provided after each repetition to simulate BCI performance.
methods_description: EEG data were acquired from 21 subjects using 16 electrodes (10-10 montage) at 512 Hz sampling rate with a g.USBamp amplifier and wet electrodes referenced to the right earlobe. Two randomized sessions (PC and VR) were conducted, each comprising 12 blocks of 5 repetitions. Each repetition consisted of 12 flashes of symbol groups in a 6×6 matrix, with target and non-target stimuli presented visually. The VR condition used a passive HMD (VRElegiant) with a Huawei Ascend Mate 7 smartphone. Visual stimulation was controlled via Unity engine to ensure consistency across modalities. Artificial random feedback (70% expected accuracy) was provided after each repetition.
